subject: Community Model Not Converging: High Number of Iterations

messages.author: 0c69c6d399345fab
messages.subject: Community Model Not Converging: High Number of Iterations
parts:
Hi all,

I have run a community model where the Y matrix represents counts for 201 taxa (aquatic insects) collected across 206 sites.Initially,  I log transformed the counts and assumed the resulting multivariate Y matrix of counts for each taxa to be normal distributed.  For MCMC, I used 4 chains,  a burn-in of 5000, and the retention of 10000 samples to estimate the posterior. These specifications resulted in a majority of Rhat values being < 1.001 for modeled parameters, and a majority of ESS values were > 10000. So overall, good convergence. 

However, being that this data is count data, I wanted to try rerunning the model and assume the multivariate count data was a consequence of a Lognormal Poisson process. For any ecological community count data, this distribution generally makes more sense given the underlying ecological processes at work. However, I was also concerned that, given the size of the matrix (201 taxa X 206 species), convergence might be very difficult to achieve if taxa counts were assumed to not be normally distributed. This logic proved to be true: I reran the model assuming a Lognormal Poisson distribution for the counts using the same MCMC specifications and a histogram indicated that estimated Rhat values ranged from 1 to 2.5 for most estimated parameters (eek!). I reran the model again; however, this time I used a burn-in of 10,000 and retained 30,000 samples to estimate the posterior for each of the 4 chains. Once again, Rhat values were awful. I could rerun the model, and increase the thinning rate, but is there a certain "cutoff" point where it makes more sense to go with the results for the previous model (i.e., where the counts were assumed to be normally distributed)? I realize this is obviously not ideal...

Sincerely,

Josh
